title: Write a custom `@FunctionalInterface` with a method `boolean test(Employee e, double threshold)` and use it as a lambda.
shortTitle: Write a custom @FunctionalInterface with boolean test(Employee e, double threshold) and use it as a lambda
keyPoints: @FunctionalInterface enforces exactly one abstract method; a second causes a compile error
A custom interface with boolean test(Employee, double) is a domain-specific two-argument predicate
A named interface like SalaryCheck is clearer and avoids autoboxing vs BiPredicate<Employee, Double>
The annotation is optional for lambda support but prevents accidental contract-breaking later
Create custom interfaces when they improve readability, avoid boxing, or need a domain-specific name
Otherwise reuse Predicate, Function, and the standard set to keep the codebase conventional

s1_definition.oneliner: A @FunctionalInterface with exactly one abstract method can be implemented by a lambda: define your own when the built-ins do not fit.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **@FunctionalInterface** tells the compiler to enforce exactly one abstract method.
- A custom `boolean test(Employee e, double threshold)` is a domain-specific two-argument predicate.
- **Named interfaces** like `SalaryCheck` are clearer than generic `BiPredicate<Employee, Double>`.
- The annotation is a **safety net**: optional for lambdas but prevents accidental contract-breaking.
- Create custom interfaces for **readability**, **primitive avoidance**, or **domain naming**.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India invents her own yes-or-no form that takes an employee and a threshold amount. Because the form has exactly one question to answer, she can fill it with a one-line lambda.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  @FunctionalInterface
  SalaryCheck { boolean test(Employee, double) }
       │
       │  Lambda: (e, t) -> e.getSalary() > t
       ▼
  SalaryCheck earnsMoreThan = (e, t) -> salary > t;

  Usage:
  earnsMoreThan.test(Rajesh, 50000)  → 75000 > 50000 = true
  earnsMoreThan.test(Amit, 50000)    → 45000 > 50000 = false
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A @FunctionalInterface with one abstract method can be implemented by a lambda. When the built-in interfaces do not fit your domain, declare a custom one like SalaryCheck with boolean test(Employee, double), which gives a domain-specific name and avoids autoboxing the primitive threshold.

The annotation tells the compiler to enforce the single-method contract, preventing someone from later adding a second abstract method and breaking all existing lambdas. At the National Bank of India, SalaryCheck was clearer than BiPredicate<Employee, Double> in the screening service.

Create custom functional interfaces when they improve readability, avoid boxing, or deserve a domain-specific name. Otherwise reuse Predicate, Function, and the standard set.

Remember one sentence: @FunctionalInterface enforces one abstract method and enables lambda implementation; create a custom one when the standard interfaces lack domain clarity or force boxing.
